questions.title: Why use WebSockets instead of HTTP?

content.text: is a communication protocol that provides a persistent, full-duplex channel over a single TCP connection. It was developed to address the limitations of HTTP. This protocol was never built for continuous, event-driven communication. The server cannot push data to the client without the client asking first, making it unsuitable for applications that require bidirectional communication. WebSocket is the go-to protocol when both the client and server need to send data through the same connection without waiting on each other. Applications that use WebSocket include live chats, multiplayer games, and collaborative editing tools.
